category: property graph (native, index-free adjacency) — 3-primary Raft cluster
notes: Neo4j 5 Enterprise (evaluation licence) with 3 primaries in one Raft cluster: the elected leader takes writes, followers replicate and reject direct writes, a new leader is elected when the leader dies. The `primary` target is a routing URI (neo4j://) so writes always reach the leader; node2/node3 are direct Bolt connections to individual members. The dataset lives in a database called `lab` (created by the harness) so it can be dropped and re-seeded from an online backup (neo4j-admin database backup + CREATE DATABASE ... seedURI). Same graph model and indexes as the Community stack. Licence: Enterprise features are used under Neo4j's evaluation terms only.

bulk_import.title: Native bulk import path (bulk API, batch, COPY-like tool)
bulk_import.detail: UNWIND $rows batches (used here); LOAD CSV; neo4j-admin database import (offline, fastest)

large_document.title: Store and read back a 15 MB document / value
large_document.detail: 15 MB string property ok (default max is bounded by page/heap, not a fixed doc size)

read_from_replica.title: Client can direct reads to a replica / secondary
read_from_replica.detail: single instance in this lab (Enterprise causal cluster routes reads to secondaries via bolt+routing)

snapshot_backup.title: Online snapshot / backup command available
snapshot_backup.detail: Community: neo4j-admin database dump needs the database stopped (STOP DATABASE is rejected, so the server stops); online backup is Enterprise

incremental_backup.title: Incremental / differential backup (file- or segment-level)
incremental_backup.detail: differential backups are Enterprise (neo4j-admin database backup --type=differential)

pitr.title: Point-in-time recovery from a continuous change log
pitr.detail: Enterprise: full + differential backups restore to a transaction id; Community has full dumps only

slow_query_log.title: Server-side slow-query log with a configurable threshold
slow_query_log.detail: query.log (db.logs.query.threshold) stays empty in Community; the in-memory query collector db.stats.collect/retrieve('QUERIES') records every query with elapsed time (status: collecting)

audit_log.title: Audit / full-query log of statements or auth events
audit_log.detail: security.log auth events and query.log are Enterprise; Community has the query collector only

structured_logs.title: JSON-structured server log out of the box
structured_logs.detail: log4j2 (conf/server-logs.xml, user-logs.xml): switch the PatternLayout to JsonTemplateLayout; text by default

runtime_log_level.title: Change log verbosity at run time (no restart)
runtime_log_level.detail: conf/server-logs.xml is re-read every 30 s (log4j2 monitorInterval) — edit the Root level, no restart; dbms.setConfigValue is Enterprise

strategy.tool: neo4j-admin database backup --from=<member>:6362 (online, from any member; --type=full|differential) into the shared /backups volume
strategy.consistency: transactionally consistent (the member's transaction log is included; `backup --type=differential` chains on the last full)
strategy.restore: cluster-wide re-seed: DROP DATABASE lab; CREATE DATABASE lab OPTIONS {existingData:'use', seedURI:'file:///backups/<tag>/<file>.backup'} WAIT — every primary seeds from the same file
strategy.incremental: differential backups (--type=differential) and `neo4j-admin database aggregate-backup` to fold them
strategy.pitr: transaction-log based (restore a full + differential chain up to a transaction id) — Enterprise
strategy.schedule: cron/CronJob running the online backup against a follower; no downtime
strategy.retention: external: prune backup directories, aggregate chains

opt01_secondary_index.title: Range scan on events(event_type, occurred_at): no index vs secondary index (both column orders)
opt01_secondary_index.what: an access path that is not indexed is a full scan; composite order matters on B-tree-like engines

opt02_projection.title: Point read of an order: whole document (with embedded items) vs 3-field projection
opt02_projection.what: returning fewer fields saves serialisation and transfer; some engines still read the whole document

opt03_pagination.title: Deep pagination: offset/skip vs keyset (cursor) at depth 10k and 100k
opt03_pagination.what: offset still walks and discards rows; a keyset cursor seeks directly into the sorted index

opt04_batching.title: Write batching: 2000 events one-by-one vs 2 bulk requests of 1000
opt04_batching.what: round trips dominate small writes; every engine has a bulk path (insert_many, pipeline, batch, _bulk)

opt05_multi_get.title: 100 point reads: sequential round trips vs one multi-get request
opt05_multi_get.what: batched reads (MGET / $in / IN / mget / pipelining) amortise the network round trip

opt06_embedding_vs_reference.title: Order with its items: embedded array (one document) vs referenced (order + items lookup)
opt06_embedding_vs_reference.what: embedding what is read together avoids a second query / join; referencing keeps documents small and items independently addressable

opt07_write_durability.title: Single-document write at each durability / write-concern level the engine offers
opt07_write_durability.what: acknowledgement level (replica acks, fsync, refresh) is the biggest lever on write latency

opt08_read_consistency.title: Point read at each read consistency level / read preference the engine offers
opt08_read_consistency.what: linearizable / quorum reads cost extra round trips; replica reads trade freshness for offload

opt09_connection_reuse.title: Point read with a new connection per operation vs one persistent client
opt09_connection_reuse.what: handshakes (TCP, TLS, auth, topology discovery) dwarf a point read; always pool

write_contention.interpretation: every accepted CAS advanced the version exactly once: atomic compare-and-set
